sources.label: CCPC determination M/23/061
sources.note: The direct regulator determination identifies the 2023-11-02 UPA, AP Novus Holding, L.P. and TIP MA Investments LP as the Apollo and Tiger investment vehicles, Novus Holdings Parent, L.P. as the indirect holder of all Modern Aviation equity, and the resulting Apollo/Tiger joint control. It does not disclose Swiss Life's treatment at closing.

sources.label: Tiger 2024 Founder-Friendly Investors release
sources.note: Tiger's manager-authored release states that in early 2024 Fund II and its co-investors fully exited Modern Aviation and that Tiger reinvested alongside Apollo through its third flagship fund and co-investors. It does not state what happened to Swiss Life.

sources.label: Tiger Modern Aviation retrospective
sources.note: Tiger's public post dates its Fund II exit to March 2024 and describes Modern Aviation at the time of exit. Any mention of Swiss Life is historical context and is not evidence of a current post-close interest.

sources.label: Apollo Infrastructure Company Q1 2024 Form 10-Q
sources.note: The direct SEC filing reports Apollo Infrastructure Company's partnership investment in Novus Holdings Parent, L.P. at 2024-03-31. It supports a disclosed Apollo investor but not an exhaustive Apollo fund roster or Swiss Life's disposition.

sources.label: AIOF III Novus Co-Invest Form D index
sources.note: The direct SEC index identifies AIOF III Novus Co-Invest (Parallel), L.P. as a filer, showing one Apollo Novus co-invest vehicle. It does not establish that AIOF III alone owns the Apollo position.

sources.label: Swiss Life 2019 Modern Aviation investment article
sources.note: The Swiss Life manager-authored article states that Swiss Life Funds (LUX) Global Infrastructure Opportunities Growth acquired a 33% Modern Aviation interest in 2019. It provides no post-March-2024 disposition or retention evidence.

sources.label: Tiger Infrastructure Partners Form ADV
sources.note: The 2026-04-30 amendment lists Swiss Life Modern Aviation Investment LP, private-fund ID 805-1072658319, with current gross asset value of $8,472,707 and two named feeders, including SLMA Investment Feeder Blocker LP with gross asset value of $7,327,259. The filing contains no portfolio-holdings schedule, cap table, distribution schedule, escrow classification, or statement that the master fund still owns Modern Aviation equity.

modelHealthOverrides: The CCPC determination is the sole application primary for the Apollo/Tiger legal ownership chain; it does not resolve Swiss Life's treatment at the March 2024 closing.

The Form ADV proves that the Swiss Life-named investment vehicle and feeders continued to report non-zero gross assets on 2026-04-30, but gross asset value and vehicle existence are not a holdings schedule and cannot be converted into current Modern Aviation equity ownership.
Tiger's Fund II exit and Fund III reinvestment disclosures must not be generalized into a conclusion about Swiss Life, a different investor.
The available direct evidence supports correcting Apollo/Tiger attribution and dates, but it does not support assigning Swiss Life an active or realized post-close state.
conclusion: The March 2024 Apollo/Tiger transition is directly supportable: AP Novus and TIP MA acquired interests in Novus Holdings Parent, Tiger Fund II exited, and Tiger Fund III and co-investors reinvested. Swiss Life's 2019 33% entry and a non-zero 2026 dedicated-vehicle gross asset value are also documented, but no direct source states whether Swiss Life sold, rolled, retained, distributed, or otherwise disposed of its Modern Aviation equity. The exact post-close Swiss Life ownership state remains a freshly evidenced exception.
